newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar firmer above 112 yen, focus on Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firmer above 112 yen, focus on Sakakibara.

text.p: *Dollar rose above 112 yen in morning Tokyo on wave of short-covering by interbank dealers and U.S. operators after testing downside in past few days.
*Stop-loss purchases near 112.00 yen and 112.30 yen pushed up greenback, dealers said.
*Market watching out for any comments by senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara, who attends seminar held by the Japan Centre for International Finance (JCIF) from 0220 GMT.
*Sakakibara is scheduled to make a speech at the seminar, which is not open to the press.
*"We have been testing the dollar's downside in the past days, so traders started to cover their short positions this morning," a dealer at a city bank said.
*He added that speculation that Sakakibara would not make yen-supportive comments at the seminar after a sharp drop in dollar against yen in past days also encouraged traders to buy back dollar.
*In cross trade, mark recovered above 65 yen in morning trade on short-covering. It stood at 65.37/40 at 0135 GMT.
*Dollar drifted higher against yen in early Tokyo trade on short-covering by Japanese interbank players and U.S. players.

*Further short-covering and possible stop-loss buying could push dollar above 112 yen temporarily, but selling interest from Japanese exporters and institutional investors likely to limit gains, dealers said.
*Dollar also edged higher versus mark in sympathy with gains in dollar/yen, but remained within narrow band, dealers said.
